correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, every length-two geodesic has same-part endpoints and is maximal. A cross-part edge is maximal exactly when both endpoint parts are singletons. Thus a complement fails exactly by containing either two vertices from a non-singleton part plus any outside vertex, or two singleton vertices. This is equivalent to the claimed two-family classification. The enumerator is a disjoint count of sparse complements and one-part complements of size at least two. Direct exhaustive checks through order ten agree.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete feasible-set description for a recent NP-hard hitting-set invariant on a canonical graph family. It exposes a genuine competition between a large single part and a sparse cross-part complement, and from that one structure obtains the minimum, all bases, and every coefficient of the size distribution. This is materially stronger than the previously published complete-bipartite scalar value and provides reusable benchmark data for transversal and packing comparisons.
